google_engineering_practices.title: Google Engineering Practices
google_engineering_practices.content:
# Google Engineering Practices

## Code Review
- Keep reviews small and focused
- Be constructive and respectful
- Look for logic errors, security issues, and performance problems
- Ensure code follows style guidelines

## Testing
- Write unit tests for all public methods
- Use integration tests for component interactions
- Aim for high code coverage
- Test edge cases and error conditions

## Documentation
- Document public APIs
- Comment complex logic
- Keep documentation up to date

## Style Guidelines
- Follow language-specific style guides
- Use consistent formatting
- Choose meaningful names

user_stories_guide.title: User Stories Guide
user_stories_guide.content:
# User Stories

## Structure
- **As a** [type of user]
- **I want** [some goal]
- **So that** [some reason]

## Acceptance Criteria
- Must be testable
- Clear and unambiguous
- Defines completion
- Business value focused

## Good Practices
- Keep stories small and focused
- Make them independent
- Negotiable and valuable
- Estimable
- Testable

## Examples
```
As a registered user,
I want to reset my password,
So that I can access my account if I forget it.

Acceptance Criteria:
- User can request password reset
- User receives reset email
- User can set new password with reset link
- Old password becomes invalid
```

solid_principles_overview.title: SOLID Principles
solid_principles_overview.content:
# SOLID Principles

## S - Single Responsibility Principle
- A class should have only one reason to change
- Each class should handle one specific responsibility

## O - Open/Closed Principle
- Software entities should be open for extension, closed for modification
- Use interfaces and abstract classes

## L - Liskov Substitution Principle
- Subtypes must be substitutable for their base types
- Don't violate the contract of the base class

## I - Interface Segregation Principle
- Many specific interfaces are better than one general interface
- Clients shouldn't depend on methods they don't use

## D - Dependency Inversion Principle
- High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules
- Both should depend on abstractions
- Abstractions shouldn't depend on details

## Benefits
- More maintainable code
- Easier testing
- Better flexibility
- Reduced coupling
